newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ARMY WARNED OF MAJOR HELICOPTER INCIDENT
The inquiry into the Blackhawk collision which killed 18 soldiers, has heard the Army was warned last year it was heading for a major incident.
The Inquiry was told the Special Air Services Regiment had concerns about the capabilities of the 5th Aviation regiment, but its commanding officer admitted there were shortfalls with
its operations.

SAS commanding officer Lieutenant Col. Michael Silverstone said he was aware of fax to him from head of the army's one division, warning the level of pilot skills had fallen and that a major safety incident was on the horizon.
And he said insufficient priority was given to flying counter-terrorism requirements.
OPPOSITION TO REEF TAX HIKE GROWING
There's increasing pressure on Canberra to abandon its plans to increase its tax on visitors to Queensland's Great Barrier Reef.
Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge has asked his state Treasury to see if tourists can be exempted from some State Government charges also applying to the reef, such as National Park entry fees.
Meanwhile the Member for Hinkler, Paul Neville will be one of six Federal MPs to meet with the Prime Minister to try to persuade him to back down on the proposed reef tax.
Mr Neville says aspects of the tax are ill-targetted and inequitable.
CONTACT BAN TODAY IN SOME GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS

Employees in two Federal Government Departments will impose work bans this morning in Queensland. Members of the Community and Public Sector Union, in the Department of Social Security and the Department of Employment and Training will ban contact with clients.
The Union's branch Secretary, Clare Moore, says the action is part of a campaign aimed at fighting the Government's plan to privatise the CES and to turn social security offices into an agency.
POSSIBLE MEDICAL BREAKTHROUGH FOR REMOTE AREAS
A remote Northern Territory community is trialling a new service that could help doctors treat patients thousands of kilometres away.
The video-conferencing link between Kintore and Adelaide's Queen Elizabeth Hospital will be officially launched this morning.
Peter Holt from Kintore says health staff at the community will use tiny cameras inserted in tubes to beam pictures of patients' skin, ears, eyes and throats to the hospital.
He says this will facilitate diagnosis, and enable health trainers to reach more of their trainees.
MARTIN BRYANT BACK IN COURT TODAY
Alleged Port Arthur gunman, Martin Bryant will be back in court today....amid tight security.
Extra police and security guards have already taken up position outside the Tasmanian Supreme Court, where all visitors will be checked by a metal detector.
Martin Bryant, who has pleaded not guilty to all 72 charges relating to the April shootings, including 35 of murder, last appeared in court on September the 30th.
His trial is due to begin next Tuesday week.
However, an appearance date was set for today to allow the Department of Public Prosecutions to discuss certain issues in the trial.
THREE MURDER APPEARANCES IN NSW
Three people will appear in courts across New South Wales today after being charged over three separate murders.
A 17-year-old male youth has been charged with the stabbing murder of a 27-year-old Smithfield man at the youth's Bosley Park home in Sydney's west yesterday morning.
The youth will appear in Lidcombe Children's Court today.
A 59-year-old man has been charged over the shooting death of a 23-year-old man at Lighting Ridge in the state's central north yesterday morning and will appear in a nearby court.
And a 23-year-old man is due in the Sutherland court, been charged over the murder last month of 22-year-old Michelle Danieletto at her Mortdale flat.
DOWNER REAFFIRMS COMMITMENT TO ASIA
Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer has reaffirmed the Federal Government's policy to engagement with Asia, saying Australia's commitment is long-term, and unshakeable.
Speaking at the Asia Australia Institute in Sydney, Mr owner said Australia is actively seeking a deeper relationship with Asia, driven by a humane approach to issues and challenges.
In a reference to the race debate fuelled by Pauline Hanson, Mr Downer said the Government rejects racism, and remains committed to a non-discriminatory immigration policy.
He appealed to all Australians to reject racist and elitist attitudes.
NEWCREST CASE CONTINUES IN THE HIGH COURT
The Commonwalth will today continue putting its case to the High Court in Canberra against a compensation claim from mining company Newcrest.
The gold mining company argues it should recieve compensation for leases held over Coronation Hill.
Coronation Hill is now part of the Commonwealth's Kakadu National Park where mining is banned.
The Commonwealth says it owes nothing to Newcrest because the company didn't have any automatic right to renew its leases and they were invalid.
It also argues the Northern Territory Government doesn't have any power to renew leases to Commonwealth land.
DOWNER REAFFIRMS COMMITMENT TO AID
Foreign Affairs Minister, Alexander Downer, has reaffirmed the Government's commitment to a substantial overseas aid program.
Mr Downer says, while there are varying degrees of opinion on the the issue of overseas aid, in the main, most Australians feel strongly about contributing to disadvantaged nations.
